title: Google Drive bounded data plane, verification and offload seam
summary: Google Drive remains primarily catalogue/durable/offload storage, but v0.1-dev7 adds executable bounded HTTP/auth/resumable/range adapters, provider-authoritative resume reconciliation, remote SHA-256 verification and optional API Client v0.3 bridging. Account lifecycle still decides whether a verified Drive location counts as durable safety.
invariants: Non-final resumable upload chunks obey the 256 KiB provider quantum; 8 MiB is the current recommended Storage chunk.
Resume and ambiguous failure recovery use provider-acknowledged Range evidence; never assume all transmitted bytes arrived.
Only provider-acknowledged bytes advance the generic transfer checkpoint; partial acknowledgement causes exact suffix replay.
Bearer/refresh credentials and resumable-session URIs are capability secrets and must not be persisted in generic catalogue/checkpoint evidence.
Google Drive sha256Checksum may verify binary Drive content before COMMIT; COPY, VERIFY and COMMIT remain separate.
Provider performance is learned from observations rather than hard-coded.
The BashQueues Drive account is disposable TEST infrastructure; a verified copy there does not automatically count as safe durability.

provenance.claim: Implements Drive HTTP/auth adapter, bounded range source, resumable sink, SHA-256 verifier and commit boundary.
Regression proves partial provider acknowledgement recovery, SHA-256 verification, capability secrecy and lifecycle-aware commit.
Regression proves optional bounded Storage HTTP request mapping onto API Client v0.3.
